diagnostics.message: aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up maps the SQS build queue to the scale_up Lambda, which requires the function's execution role to be able to ReceiveMessage/DeleteMessage on the queue. That permission is only granted by aws_iam_role_policy.scale_up (lambda-scale-up.json with sqs_arn), but the event source mapping has no dependency on it (its only deps are the Lambda and the queue). Lambda validates the role's SQS permissions synchronously on CreateEventSourceMapping, so if the mapping is created before the policy is attached the apply fails with "The provided execution role does not have permissions to call ReceiveMessage on SQS". Add depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy.scale_up] to the event source mapping.

aws_s3_object.trigger is the one-shot deploy trigger: uploading it to the distribution bucket is immediately delivered by aws_s3_bucket_notification.on_deploy to the syncer Lambda so the runner binary is synced up front. The syncer Lambda needs its S3 write permission (aws_iam_role_policy.syncer, which grants PutObject on the action_dist bucket) to perform that sync, but the trigger's dependency chain (notification -> lambda permission -> lambda/bucket) does not include that policy. If the trigger fires before the role policy is attached, the initial invocation fails and the binary is not synced until the hourly scheduled rule runs. Add depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy.syncer] to aws_s3_object.trigger.
